component.name: DeeCure
component.summary: Deep insight into every layer of your computer

description.p: DeeCure gives deep insight into every layer of your computer: sensor limits, PCIe links, firmware, kernel settings, and services. It warns on the hardware's own limits, explains everything in plain words, and fixes problems safely.

ul.li: A health score and a short list of problems, most serious first
Health warnings judged against each part's own limits: CPU, drives, graphics, battery, memory, disks, network, and security; never about normal use, and you can change every limit
Deep hardware details: sensors and their limits, drives and their links, graphics, firmware, USB and PCIe, screens, and every wake-up source
Battery and power controls: charge limits, charge mode, turbo, CPU speed on battery, sleep type, lid action, and device power saving, kept after restart
An Optimize page that scans this computer live and offers only what it measurably needs
Safe fixes with a preview of every step, a check that they worked, and undo
A timeline of what changed: updates, config files, devices, crashes, and hardware errors
Notifications for serious problems, quiet hours, and a weekly summary
Beginner, Advanced, and Expert views: light for newcomers, every detail for experts
Updates checked daily, weekly, or never, installed after your OK or automatically, each package checked first

description.p: Nothing about this computer is sent anywhere, and there is no account. The only connection is a daily check for DeeCure updates on GitHub, which you can turn off.

A new Optimize page: a round Scan button checks this computer live, part by part, a ring shows what passed and what needs something, and the improvements come one by one with what was measured. It checks by itself only once a day, and the Overview shows how many improvements wait.

Shows which apps used the battery, CPU, memory, and internet over time, and makes DeeCure lighter: nothing is read while its window is hidden, and the newest readings and the temperature sensors cost far less.
Fixes updating DeeCure from the app and automatic updates, which stopped half way because the new package stopped the service installing it.

Safety release. Kernel and other updates through DeeCure no longer stop half way, updates never remove other packages and keep settings files you changed, clean-ups that would remove the desktop are refused, the session and login screen are never restarted or ended, turning the firewall on keeps SSH connected, and power settings that can freeze some computers are skipped after a start that froze.

Every page is easier to read: a short summary first, then bars, tiles, and charts, with full tables under Show all. A warning now marks the exact sub-page and the panel that shows it, and open issues are cards with Open and Fix. Fewer false warnings: the disk forecast handles a laptop that sleeps, heat slowdowns count only while the CPU is hot, the firewall warning leaves out Docker's ports, and a warning that cannot be confirmed for a day closes.

Admin details read with your password: memory slots, BIOS settings, NVMe details, drive self-tests, measured chip power, deep-sleep time, wake-ups per process, sudo rules, and the SSH server's real settings. Two new warnings from a daily check: a drive wearing out, and SSH letting root sign in with a password.

Beginner, Advanced, and Expert views with deep hardware and system details; about 50 health warnings judged against each part's own limits, with your own limits in Settings; battery and power controls kept after restart; an Optimize page; and updates that check themselves and install after your OK.
The agent starts right after installing, so the app works without signing out and in again.
First pre-release, for testing: every page shows real data from this computer, with safe fixes, a what-changed timeline, disk forecasts, notifications, and a weekly summary.
